Followed by required sea service, competency certification and pilot training.
Ship manoeuvring, port approaches, harbour safety and vessel movement.

sections.heading: What does a Marine Pilot do?

blocks.text: A Marine Pilot, also called a harbour pilot or port pilot, guides ships safely into and out of ports, through channels and other restricted waterways. They bring specialised knowledge of local tides, currents, depths, navigational hazards and port procedures.

A Marine Pilot is different from a ship's deck officer: the pilot provides local navigation and manoeuvring expertise, while the ship's master retains overall command and responsibility for the vessel.

items.text: Board vessels and brief the master on the intended passage and manoeuvres.
Guide ships through port channels, narrow waterways and berthing or unberthing operations.
Assess weather, tides, currents, visibility, traffic and under-keel clearance.
Coordinate with tugboats, port control, vessel traffic services and mooring teams.
Respond to changing conditions and help prevent collisions, groundings and port accidents.
Follow port-specific pilotage rules, safety procedures and reporting requirements.

blocks.text: Consider a recognised B.Sc. Nautical Science programme or Diploma in Nautical Science (DNS). Eligibility, medical fitness, sponsorship and admission requirements must be checked against current Indian maritime rules.
Complete the required pre-sea training and onboard sea service, progressing through deck cadet and deck officer roles as eligible.
Obtain the required Certificates of Competency and accumulate the relevant experience, potentially progressing to senior officer and master-level responsibilities.
Meet the relevant port authority's eligibility criteria, complete pilot assessment and local familiarisation, and obtain the required authorisation for the port or pilotage district.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Marine Pilot is generally a later-career maritime role, not a direct job after graduation. Required sea service, officer rank, competency certificates and pilotage authorisation vary by jurisdiction and port. There is no single guaranteed timeline from college to becoming a pilot.

The most important distinction for this career is that a nautical degree is the starting point, while a Marine Pilot licence requires additional professional qualifications and port-specific experience. India's Directorate General of Shipping outlines the deck-officer pathway, and its nautical examination guidance describes pilot-licensing requirements.
Stage A — Before and during college

items.text: Build strong knowledge of mathematics, physics, geography and English communication.
Study navigation, chartwork, tides, meteorology and maritime safety.
Practise nautical calculations, position plotting and basic ship-handling concepts.
Develop fitness, discipline, teamwork and the ability to stay calm under pressure.
Check medical and eyesight standards before committing to the programme.
Confirm that the institute and course are currently approved by India's Directorate General of Shipping (DG Shipping).
